resolution: Captured the baseline edit-latency matrix from the user's run (place ~540ms total, move/rotate ~420ms; place's gesture→push 160ms vs move's ~0ms) and read it: there are two costs — a ~160ms place-only reconcile, and a ~380-420ms post-push main-thread block that hits EVERY verb (the rAF can't fire until the host frees up; the PLACEFREEZE deferred snapshot of ~90ms/commit across 12 streams is part of it). To attack precisely instead of guessing, shipped a phase breakdown of the timer (cart-side, hot-reloads): each edit now logs total = pre (gesture→effect: onCommit + parent stream apply + reconcile) + scans (the loader's O(N) overlay rebuild: pieceInstanceRows + meshPropLivePush + buildingSkinBoxes) + push (host door calls) + host-block (push→next frame: snapshot/re-render/GPU upload). One place-click now prints exactly where the ~540ms goes, so the next optimization targets the dominant phase. Sha b42e818cd. Next: read the breakdown, then kill the biggest phase end-to-end.
